changelog: fix: attaching the phylogenetic tree was throwing away most of the ASV table, so the chart editor and the Word report have been answering the same question with different numbers. viz_pipeline.R called merge_phyloseq(ps, phy_tree(tr)). phyloseq intersects the taxa with the tree's tips, and dada2_pipeline.R caps the tree at the top 500 ASVs by abundance because aligning more is slow — a sensible cap. The effect was that ps silently went from 1330 ASVs to 500, and EVERYTHING this script then wrote into r_tables/ was computed on those 500: alpha diversity, Bray-Curtis and Jaccard, PCoA and NMDS, rarefaction, prevalence, and the taxonomy tables the chart editor reads. report_builder.py reads the job root instead and used all 1330. On U2Bio-139-v144Genus that is Observed = 222 / 585 / 275 / 675 in the Word report against 133 / 295 / 168 / 295 in the chart editor — verified by recomputing both from asv_table.csv and phylo_tree.nwk, which reproduces each file exactly. Nothing in either output said which population it described, and the log line read 'Attached phylogenetic tree' while 830 ASVs left the analysis. The cap on the tree is fine; pruning the DATA to it is not. ps now stays full width and a separate ps_tree carries the tree. The three places that genuinely need one use it and say how much of the table it covers: Faith's PD (its matrix and its tree now come from the same object, which they did not have to before), UniFrac, and the ggtree figure — that figure read phy_tree(ps) and would otherwise have found nothing and skipped itself without explanation. The QIIME2 path had the same bug in a different spelling, phy_tree(ps) <- read_tree(file), which prunes the same way; fixed with it. This one needs a re-run to take effect — the numbers in an existing result folder were written by the old code. Until then, treat the chart editor's diversity figures for any existing job as covering the top 500 ASVs, not the whole table.
